newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Cytec to restructure Dutch chemical plants. [CORRECTED 15:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Cytec to restructure Dutch chemical plants. [CORRECTED 15:55 GMT]

text.p: U.S. industrial chemicals maker Cytec said on Friday it planned to restructure its Dutch operations with the net loss of 100 jobs.
"The restructuring forms part of an efficiency drive to cut costs in the face of continued downward pressure on margins," said Mark Goyens, spokesman for Cytec Industries BV.

The two-year programme involves the modernisation of Cytec's two existing plants, which manufacture specialty chemicals for the paper and water treatment industries and acrylamide monomers, a semi-manufacture used in coatings. In addition Cytec will build a new 31 million guilder benzotriazol plant.
Benzotriazol is a polymer additive which absorbs ultraviolet radiation and so stabilises the colour of plastics.
Costs of the plant modernisation are estimated at 20 million guilders, but Goyens said it was too early to put a figure on the total restructuring cost.

Goyens said the restructuring would lead to the loss of 81 jobs next year and a further 31 in 1998 of a 340-strong workforce. The new benzotriazol plant, due to come on-stream in 1998, will employ 15.
Cytec Industries BV functions as the company's European head-office.
The company also has a manufacturing operation in Bradford, Britain. Its European operations turn over an estimated $160 million a year.
(Corrects to show U.S. dollars instead of guilders for turnover figure).
